title: Python SDK: slim streaming bridge + adaptive checkpoint UX
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, low-allocation "slim bridge" adapter in the Python SDK that unifies server-sent-event (SSE) and gRPC streaming responses into a single async-iterator surface with ergonomic hooks for checkpointing, backpressure, and event transformation. The goal is to provide a developer-friendly default that supports resumability and safe retries at fragment boundaries, while giving teams pluggable extension points (transformers, checkpoint policy, telemetry hooks) for advanced use cases.
acceptance_criteria: Async iterator API exposing events and incremental text fragments with a clear commit/checkpoint API
Default adapter implements bounded buffer + watermark-based backpressure to avoid OOM under high fan-in
Resume semantics: able to restart a stream from a server-provided checkpoint token and rehydrate local state
Pluggable event transformer contract documented and exercised in examples
Tests cover retry-at-fragment-boundary, idempotent consumer tests, and telemetry emission for queue/backpressure events
Minimal allocations in hot path measured (benchmark < 10% overhead vs raw SSE handler in microbench)
Docs include two recipes: (1) simple chat consumer (one-liner) and (2) composable consumer with checkpoint persistence
technical_design: Adapter wraps raw transport (SSE/gRPC) readers and exposes an async generator that yields typed event tuples (kind, payload, fragment_offset). A small fixed-size asyncio.Queue acts as the bounded buffer. Backpressure is implemented with a watermark (high/low); when high-watermark is reached the adapter applies a transport-level pause (if supported) or drops non-essential meta events and signals a backpressure telemetry event. Checkpoints are signed tokens emitted by the server or synthesized by the adapter at safe fragment boundaries. The consumer can call adapter.commit(checkpoint_token) to advance durable progress. Transformer hooks are sync or async callables that can mutate events; they run off the main hot path when possible via short-lived tasks. Telemetry hooks emit queue depth, fragment-latency, retry attempts, and checkpoint commits to the SDK tracer.
implementation_plan: 1) RFC + API sketch: finalize public surface for AsyncChatStream (3 days)
2) Core adapter: implement transport-agnostic reader + bounded queue + watermarks (4 days)
3) Checkpoint contract: server token parsing, commit API, and persisted example (2 days)
4) Transformer & hooks: pluggable interfaces + simple built-ins (2 days)
5) Tests & benchmarks: microbench for allocations, integration tests for resume/retry (3 days)
6) Docs & examples: add two cookbooks and update quickstart (2 days)
7) Review + iterate based on SDK lead feedback (1 day)
risks: Server platforms do not provide a consistent checkpoint token; we need a safe client-side fallback that is still resumable
Transport pause semantics are inconsistent across environments (SSE vs gRPC web); implementing a robust pause/resume fallback increases complexity
Telemetry volume from per-fragment events could be noisy; must provide sampling and aggregation defaults
Making transformer hooks async may introduce ordering surprises if not well-documented
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter queue watermarks and pause/resume behavior
Integration test that simulates mid-stream failure and successful resume using checkpoint token
Property test for idempotence: reprocessing from last committed checkpoint yields no duplicate visible output
Benchmark comparing allocations and latency vs existing raw stream helper (target <10% overhead)
End-to-end example test that persists checkpoints to a local file and demonstrates resume
comments: 2026-02-22: Spike completed. POC demonstrates resume from server checkpoint and bounded queue backpressure. Observed increased latency when transformers are applied inline.

2026-02-27: Design review with PM and DX. Agreed on default conservative telemetry sampling and a small public API: AsyncChatStream + commit() + transform hook. PM requested a one-line helper for quickstarts.

2026-03-03: Implementation 60% done. Core adapter and queue in place. Added a transport pause abstraction; SSE pause uses client-side drain, gRPC uses flow-control if available. Benchmarks show ~7% allocation overhead on microbench.
2026-03-08: Code review feedback from SDK lead: make transform hook opt-in and ensure ordering guarantees in docs. Added tests for async transformer ordering.
2026-03-10: Unblocked on telemetry sampling; working on packaging examples and adding checkpoint persistence recipe. Next: finalize PR and schedule cross-team demo.
